findings.summary: The warrant was deleted: the sentence that gives participant, critic, and heir standing to name a betrayal in the text's own words.

evidence.baseline: We have written them here, in the body of the text, precisely so that they function as a standard: if Providence ever begins to measure worth, to score belief, to rank persons against one another, to render permanent verdicts, or to reach into the whole of a life, then it has crossed the line into the very thing this chapter forswears, and everyone (participant, critic, and heir) holds the warrant, in these words, to name it as the betrayal it would be and to act accordingly.
evidence.shipped: The refusal to measure these domains is not a feature waiting for a future product decision. It is part of the institution's right to exist.

findings.diagnosis: The shipped half keeps the right-to-exist claim and drops the warrant, which is the committing half: it names who may act and on what authority. The same cautious-half shape as everywhere else in the volume. Restored, with the everyone triple fenced in parentheses where the baseline used a dash pair around a comma-bearing list.

findings.summary: The five refusals lost their reasons; the enumerated worth argument was reduced to a list of nouns.

evidence.baseline: Providence does not measure a person's worth. The coherence record reflects how someone has shown up in particular encounters; it makes no claim, and can make no claim, about the value of a human being, which is not a measurable quantity and is held, in the founding commitments of this project, to be infinite and equal in every person regardless of any record.
evidence.shipped: Providence does not measure worth, conscience, belief, political conviction, or the whole of a life.

findings.diagnosis: Each baseline refusal carries its warrant: worth is unmeasurable and held infinite and equal, conviction is sovereign, ranking is refused for trajectory-against-own-past, verdicts are refused because the record honors growth, and unentered domains stay unseen. The shipped list asserts the refusals without the commitments that make them checkable. Restored in full.

findings.summary: The pass's opacity paragraph and inference bound are preserved for ratification.

evidence.shipped: It should not infer them indirectly from intimate signals. ... Sovereignty also includes the right to opacity. A person may choose not to explain a physiological change, disclose a feeling, or turn every encounter into data. Human dignity includes parts of the self that no system is entitled to make legible.

findings.authorizedBy: Preservation; cut from prose as seeded canon rather than repair.
findings.diagnosis: The inference bound closes a real gap: the baseline forbids measuring belief but not inferring it, and modern models make the difference material. The right-to-opacity paragraph is the strongest pass-authored doctrine in the chapter and extends sovereignty beyond anything the baseline claims. Both are new canon, which drafting cannot seed without a decision; preserved verbatim for the author, flagged as worth adopting.

evidence.baseline: The never-to-measure mark, the everyone fence, and the display-line fence.

findings.diagnosis: The never-to-measure mark opened the second movement of the opening sentence and became a period with And. The everyone fence held a comma-bearing triple and became parentheses. The display-line fence held the enumeration of unmeasured things and became a colon, with the corrective movement (Not because it has not yet gotten to them, but because the refusal is the condition of its existence) standing as its own earned fragment, a display-matter landing the voice card permits.
